neighbours.label: the boundary (' than' or the sentence-final period) of a claim that some group is more likely to have an outcome or that a condition leads to a consequence
fire: Smokers are far more likely to develop gum disease than people who never smoked.
Children who skip breakfast are more likely to feel tired by noon.
Older drivers are more likely to have accidents at night than during the day.
People who sleep badly are more likely to catch a cold.
Babies born early are more likely to need help breathing than other babies.
Workers who sit all day are more likely to suffer back pain.
Cats kept indoors are less likely to pick up fleas than outdoor cats.
Runners who skip stretching are more likely to injure a knee.
quiet: Smokers often stand outside the office during the morning break.
Children who skip breakfast usually eat a big lunch at school.
Older drivers often drive slowly on the motorway at night.
People who sleep badly often drink coffee in the morning.
Babies born early often spend a few weeks in a special ward.
Workers who sit all day often walk home in the evening.
Cats kept indoors often sleep on the sofa all afternoon.
Runners who skip stretching usually start their run with a slow jog.
